contract.words: Collect $4,000 of settled cash within 75 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $4000 of cash settled in the owner's account within 21 days

strategy.title: Deliver the five signed OASIS documentation reviews through ClearChart and collect $6,000 net-45
strategy.why: Five home health agencies have each given written acceptance at $1,200 for a pre-billing OASIS documentation review ($6,000 total, 4 of 5 suffice for $4,000). ClearChart Coding Services quoted $600 a review and can complete all five within 10 days of the order. Delivered by day 11, invoiced on delivery, paid net-45: cash settles by day 56 of 75. ClearChart is paid from the receipts, so no capital is tied up (card exposure $0); each deal keeps $600.

alternatives.title: Deliver only four reviews
alternatives.why: 4 × $1,200 = $4,800 also meets the target, but all five are signed and profitable, so delivering five adds margin against a slipped payment.

steps.label: Confirm the five signed orders with each agency administrator and schedule document access
Order the five reviews from ClearChart Coding Services at its quoted $600 a review
ClearChart completes and delivers the five OASIS pre-billing reviews; Brain invoices each agency on delivery
Collect the five $1,200 invoices at net-45

sources.claim: Five written acceptances, each AGREED at $1,200 for the OASIS pre-billing review
ClearChart Coding Services quoted $600 a review and can complete all five within 10 days of the order
45 days to usable cash (paid net-45 after delivery)

strategy.title: No plan: the five signed reviews settle net-45, after the new 21-day deadline
strategy.why: The goal's window is now 21 days. The five signed OASIS reviews ($6,000 at $1,200, ClearChart fulfils at $600 within 10 days) are invoiced on delivery and paid net-45, so the earliest cash arrives about day 45-56, after day 21. Inside the window this opening settles $0 of the $4,000.

alternatives.title: Deliver the five signed reviews anyway
alternatives.why: Still worth $6,000 gross (net $3,000) but it settles around day 56, outside a 21-day window.

alternatives.title: Ask the agencies to pay on delivery
alternatives.why: Nothing on the record shows any agency accepting shorter terms; the signed terms are net-45.

steps.label: Ask whether the five signed agencies will pay on delivery or early, or find openings that settle inside 21 days

answers.finding: Target reading: the plan meets $4,000 on settled cash collected ($6,000), which is the contract's SETTLED_CASH metric. Net of the supplier it keeps $3,000. With 4 deals it nets $2,400. The owner should know that the money kept is below $4,000 even though collections exceed it.
answers.resolution: No longer applicable: no cash settles inside the 21-day window under either reading.

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE holds on the record. Five WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $1,200 each are AGREED by the five named agencies, so the price is a real purchase price these buyers committed to. Fulfilment is by the recorded fulfiller, ClearChart Coding Services, which quoted $600 a review and all five within 10 days (EVIDENCE). Direct cost of $600 is below the price, and exposure is $0 (EVIDENCE). Net-45 after delivery is the evidenced settlement. Recomputed: 5 x $1,200 = $6,000 collected; delivery by day 11 + 45 = day 56, inside 75; supplier cost 5 x $600 = $3,000, paid from receipts on day 56; checker max exposure $0. Four acceptances alone give $4,800 gross, so one slipped agency still leaves the target met on collections.
findings: Arithmetic: $6,000 settled by day 56 of 75; supplier $3,000; net $3,000 after paying ClearChart.

Target reading: the plan meets $4,000 on settled cash collected ($6,000), which is the contract's SETTLED_CASH metric. Net of the supplier it keeps $3,000. With 4 deals it nets $2,400. The owner should know that the money kept is below $4,000 even though collections exceed it.

Zero-capital rests on paying ClearChart from receipts at day 56. The card's exposure $0 is EVIDENCE and nothing on the record contradicts it, but ClearChart's payment terms are not stated in its quote. Confirm pay-when-paid (or net-45+) terms in writing before step s2. If ClearChart requires payment on delivery (day 11), $3,000 is tied up for 45 days and breaks the no-up-front-capital limit.
PAY_A_SUPPLIER shows NOT_DECLARED, and SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE show NOT_CONNECTED. They must be set up before day 1.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is correct under the changed contract, which shortened the window from 75 to 21 days. The only opening's five signed agreements ($1,200 each, $6,000) are invoiced on delivery and paid net-45 (EVIDENCE timeToFirstCash 45 days; the agreements' deliverable text says net-45). ClearChart needs up to 10 days to deliver. Recomputed: the earliest settlement is about day 45 (delivery on day 0) and realistically day 55-56, both after day 21, so $0 of the $4,000 settles inside the window. This is a genuine constraint: even with every piece of evidence in hand and every buyer agreeing, the signed terms put the cash outside the limit. The plan names it as a DEADLINE constraint with decisive link SETTLES_IN_TIME, and Brain's planner independently reads it as infeasible as stated. Not assuming pay-on-delivery terms, which nothing on the record supports, is correct.
findings: Arithmetic: 10 days' delivery + 45 days' terms = day 55-56 settlement against a 21-day window; inside the window, $0 of the $4,000.

Constraint suggestion (window of at least 56 days) is consistent with the evidence. Brain's own 45-day figure assumes delivery on day 0, which the 10-day fulfilment quote does not support, so 56 is the safer number to give the owner.

Delivering anyway still nets $3,000 ($6,000 - 5 x $600) around day 56, but only if ClearChart accepts payment from receipts. Its payment terms remain unstated, and paying it on delivery would break the $0 exposure limit.
Asking the agencies for pay-on-delivery terms is a legitimate next step. Any accepted change should be recorded as a new written agreement before it is planned on.
